findings.title: Fallback translations can be permanently cached as missing
findings.body: I18n.translate only loads config.locale before consulting the LRU cache, not the fallback locales configured in config/initializers/i18n.rb. If a no-argument translation is first looked up when its fallback locale (site default or :en) has not been loaded, translate_no_cache returns a 'translation missing' string and lines 71-76 freeze and cache it under the current locale. Loading the fallback locale later does not invalidate @cache, so the missing-translation string keeps being served until LRU eviction or reload, defeating the fallback feature.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests
findings.body: ensure_loaded! is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale. Server-side translations also happen in background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console and model code, where no controller before_filter runs. In those contexts I18n.translate loads only the current locale, so keys missing from that locale but present in the site-default or English files return 'translation missing' instead of falling back, making the feature inconsistent between requests and jobs/mailers.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList breaks the I18n.fallbacks Hash contract
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to ignore anything stored in the hash and always synthesize a value. Code using the documented I18n fallbacks API, e.g. I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:fr] or the Fallbacks#map helper provided by the i18n gem/Rails, will write entries that are never read back, and enumeration/keys/empty? report an empty hash even though [] returns entries. Per-locale fallback customization is therefore silently discarded.

findings.title: Every fallback lookup queries SiteSetting and crashes if it is unset
findings.body: The i18n Fallbacks backend calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on each translation lookup, and this implementation calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time. That ties hot-path translation (including translations with arguments, which bypass the accelerator cache) to the DB-backed settings store, adds a settings lookup per translation, breaks translations performed before the database/settings are available (boot, migrations), and raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil instead of degrading to :en.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback ordering or loading behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a custom FallbackLocaleList, a new I18n.ensure_loaded!, and a per-request loading hook, and removes the Rails config.i18n.fallbacks settings, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that a missing key in the user locale resolves to the site-default then English text, that duplicate locales (user == default == :en) are de-duplicated, or that fallback files are loaded in non-controller contexts, so the cache-poisoning and jobs/mailers gaps above can regress undetected.
